questions.question: The marks obtained by 11 students in a mathematics test are as follows: 45, 62, 58, 71, 66, 54, 60, 49, 68, 57, 63. What is the median marks?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total observations = 11 (odd number)

Median position = (11 + 1) ÷ 2 = 6th term

Arrange numbers mentally and pick middle value

6th value = 60

**∴ Answer = 60**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 45, 62, 58, 71, 66, 54, 60, 49, 68, 57, 63

**Formula used:** Median = (n + 1) ÷ 2 th term (for odd n)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Arrange in ascending order: 45, 49, 54, 57, 58, 60, 62, 63, 66, 68, 71

⇒ n = 11

⇒ Median position = (11 + 1) ÷ 2 = 6

⇒ 6th term = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median for Even Number of Observations

Median = average of (n ÷ 2)th and (n ÷ 2 + 1)th terms

Mean vs Median

Mean = sum of observations ÷ total observations, while median is the middle value

Mode

Mode is the value that occurs most frequently in the dataset

Effect of Extreme Values

Median is not affected by very large or small values, unlike mean

questions.question: At what rate (in percentage) per year will a sum of money double itself in 20 years on simple interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For doubling in Simple Interest, Interest = Principal

So, SI = P ⇒ (P × R × T) ÷ 100 = P

Cancel P ⇒ (R × 20) ÷ 100 = 1

R = 100 ÷ 20 = 5%

**∴ Answer = 5%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time = 20 years, Amount = 2P

**Formula used:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since amount doubles ⇒ SI = Amount − Principal = P

⇒ So, P = (P × R × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ Cancel P from both sides

⇒ 1 = (R × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 20 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount Formula

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

Doubling Time (SI)

Time required to double = 100 ÷ Rate

Rule of 72 (CI concept)

Doubling time ≈ 72 ÷ Rate (used in Compound Interest)

questions.question:
What is the nature of the roots of the following quadratic equation?

x-(1)/(x)=17
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply both sides by x ⇒ x² − 1 = 17x

Rearrange ⇒ x² − 17x − 1 = 0

Check discriminant sign: b² − 4ac = (−17)² − 4(1)(−1)

= 289 + 4 = 293 > 0 and not a perfect square

**∴ Roots are real, distinct and irrational**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x − 1/x = 17

**Formula used:**

Discriminant D = b² − 4ac

**Calculations:**

⇒ Multiply both sides by x ⇒ x² − 1 = 17x

⇒ Rearranging ⇒ x² − 17x − 1 = 0

⇒ Here, a = 1, b = −17, c = −1

⇒ D = (−17)² − 4 × 1 × (−1)

⇒ D = 289 + 4 = 293

⇒ Since D > 0 and not a perfect square

**∴ The correct answer is real, distinct and irrational roots.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots (Discriminant)

If D > 0 → real and distinct, D = 0 → real and equal, D < 0 → complex roots

Perfect Square Condition

If D is a perfect square, roots are rational; otherwise irrational

Forming Quadratic from Fraction

Equations like x − 1/x = k can be converted to x² − kx − 1 = 0

Sum and Product of Roots

Sum = −b/a and Product = c/a for ax² + bx + c = 0

questions.question: The 24th Constitutional Amendment gave the Parliament which of the following powers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amend Fundamental Rights**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **24th Constitutional Amendment Act** was enacted in the year **1971** during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**. This amendment was primarily brought to nullify the effect of the **Supreme Court** judgment in the **Golaknath case (1967)**.
 
• It amended **Article 13** and **Article 368** of the **Constitution of India** to affirm that **Parliament** has the absolute power to amend any part of the Constitution, including **Fundamental Rights** listed in **Part III**. *Hence, option A is correct.*
 
• The amendment clarified that **Article 13**, which states that any law inconsistent with **Fundamental Rights** shall be void, would not apply to any constitutional amendment made under **Article 368**.
 
• Prior to this, the **Supreme Court** in the **Golaknath case** had ruled that **Parliament** could not abridge or take away any of the **Fundamental Rights** through a constitutional amendment.
 
• The power to suspend **High Court** judgments or bypass judicial proceedings is not a feature of the **24th Amendment**; such issues were more relevant to the **42nd Amendment** or specific emergency provisions. *Hence, option B is incorrect.*
 
• While the amendment sought to limit the scope of **Judicial Review** over constitutional changes, it did not entirely "override" the concept of judicial review, which was later protected as a part of the **Basic Structure**. *Hence, option C is incorrect.*
 
• The **24th Amendment** does not deal with the suspension of **elections**, which is governed by the **Representation of the People Act** and **Emergency** provisions of the **Constitution**. *Hence, option D is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 368:** This article provides the **Parliament** with the constituent power to amend the **Constitution** by way of addition, variation, or repeal of any provision according to the procedure laid down therein.
 
• **President's Assent:** The **24th Amendment** made it mandatory for the **President of India** to give his assent to a **Constitution Amendment Bill**. Before this, the **President** had the discretion to withhold assent or return the bill.
 
• **Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967):** In this landmark **6:5** majority judgment, the **Supreme Court** held that **Fundamental Rights** are "transcendental" and "immutable," meaning **Parliament** has no power to amend them. This created a legal deadlock that the **24th Amendment** resolved.
 
• **Article 13:** It originally acted as a shield for **Fundamental Rights**, declaring that any "law" made by the state that takes away these rights is void. The **24th Amendment** added a clause stating that "nothing in this article shall apply to any amendment of this Constitution made under **Article 368**."
 
• **Legislative Supremacy:** This amendment represented a period of intense conflict between the **Judiciary** and the **Legislature** in **India**, where the government sought to establish the supremacy of **Parliament** in matters of social and economic reform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973):** The validity of the **24th Amendment** was challenged in this famous case. The **Supreme Court** upheld the amendment but introduced the **Basic Structure Doctrine**, stating that while **Parliament** can amend any part of the **Constitution**, it cannot alter its "basic structure" or "essential features."
 
• **Fundamental Rights vs. DPSP:** The **24th Amendment** was a precursor to the **25th Amendment**, which sought to give **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** precedence over **Fundamental Rights** in certain cases (specifically **Articles 39(b)** and **39(c)**).
 
• **Constitutional Balance:** Today, the power of **Parliament** to amend the **Constitution** is widely accepted, provided it respects the core values like **Secularism**, **Democracy**, **Federalism**, and **Judicial Review** as established by the **13-judge bench** in **1973**.
 
• The amendment effectively changed the status of **Fundamental Rights** from being unalterable to being amendable, ensuring that the **Constitution** remains a living document capable of adapting to the changing needs of the **Indian** people.

questions.question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 32° more than the smaller. The smaller angle (in degree) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Supplementary angles sum = 180°

Let smaller = x ⇒ larger = x + 32

So, x + (x + 32) = 180

2x = 148 ⇒ x = 74

**∴ Answer = 74°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two supplementary angles = 180°, difference = 32°

**Formula used:**

Sum = 180°, Let angles be a and b such that a + b = 180

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let smaller angle = x

⇒ Larger angle = x + 32

⇒ x + (x + 32) = 180

⇒ 2x + 32 = 180

⇒ 2x = 148

⇒ x = 74

**∴ The correct answer is 74°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles whose sum is 180° are called supplementary angles

Complementary Angles

Two angles whose sum is 90° are called complementary angles

Linear Pair

A linear pair of angles always adds up to 180°

General Formula

If difference is d, smaller angle = (180 − d) ÷ 2

questions.question: A man can row at 8 km/hr in still water. When the river flows at 2 km/hr, he takes 3 hours 12 minutes to row to a destination and back. Find the distance to the destination.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = 8 + 2 = 10 km/hr, Upstream speed = 8 − 2 = 6 km/hr

Total time = 3 hr 12 min = 3.2 hr

Round trip time formula: Time = 2D × (1/10 + 1/6)

⇒ 3.2 = 2D × (16/60) = 2D × (4/15)

D = 6 km

**∴ Answer = 6 km**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed in still water = 8 km/hr

Stream speed = 2 km/hr

Total time = 3 hr 12 min = 3.2 hr

**Formula used:**

Downstream speed = u + v

Upstream speed = u − v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed = 8 + 2 = 10 km/hr

⇒ Upstream speed = 8 − 2 = 6 km/hr

⇒ Let distance = D km

⇒ Time downstream = D ÷ 10

⇒ Time upstream = D ÷ 6

⇒ Total time = D/10 + D/6 = 3.2

⇒ Taking LCM 30 ⇒ (3D + 5D) ÷ 30 = 3.2

⇒ 8D ÷ 30 = 3.2

⇒ 4D ÷ 15 = 3.2

⇒ D = (3.2 × 15) ÷ 4 = 48 ÷ 4 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream = u + v, Upstream = u − v where u = still water speed and v = stream speed

Round Trip Time

Total time = Distance/Downstream + Distance/Upstream

LCM Method

Use LCM of denominators to simplify fractional equations quickly

Unit Conversion

Always convert minutes into hours: minutes ÷ 60

questions.question: What is the chemical reaction responsible for the leavening of bread, where carbon dioxide is produced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fermentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fermentation** is a metabolic process that produces chemical changes in organic substrates through the action of **enzymes**. In the context of bread making, it refers specifically to the process where **yeast** (primarily **Saccharomyces cerevisiae**) converts **sugars** (glucose, fructose, and sucrose) into **ethanol** and **carbon dioxide (CO2)**.
 
• The **carbon dioxide** gas produced during this reaction is trapped within the dough by the **gluten** network. As the gas expands, it causes the dough to rise, a process known as **leavening**. This creates the light, airy texture characteristic of bread.
 
• The chemical equation for this **anaerobic** process can be represented as: **C6H12O6 (glucose) → 2C2H5OH (ethanol) + 2CO2 (carbon dioxide)**. While ethanol is also produced, it mostly **evaporates** during the baking process at **high temperatures**.
 
• Fermentation is highly sensitive to **temperature** and **moisture**. Most bread yeasts work optimally between **25°C to 35°C**. Temperatures above **50°C** typically kill the yeast cells, stopping the fermentation process.
 
• Apart from leavening, fermentation contributes significantly to the **flavor** and **aroma** of the bread due to the production of organic acids and other **by-products** during the breakdown of sugars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxidation-Reduction Reaction:** While **redox reactions** occur during dough mixing (impacting the **disulfide bonds** in gluten proteins), they are not the primary mechanism for leavening. Oxidation helps in **strengthening the dough**, but does not produce the gas required for rising.
 
• **Enzymatic Reaction:** In bread making, **amylase enzymes** are crucial as they break down **starch** into **maltose** and **glucose**. This provides the **substrate** (food) for the yeast to perform fermentation. However, the production of CO2 itself is the result of the fermentation pathway rather than a simple enzymatic hydrolysis.
 
• **Acid-Base Reaction:** This is the mechanism used in **chemical leavening** rather than biological leavening. It involves the reaction between an **acid** (like buttermilk or cream of tartar) and a **base** (like **sodium bicarbonate/baking soda**) to release **carbon dioxide** quickly. This is common in cakes and biscuits but not traditional yeast bread.
 
• **Role of Gluten:** Gluten is a **protein complex** formed from **gliadin** and **glutenin** when flour is mixed with **water**. It provides the **elasticity** and **extensibility** necessary to hold the **gas bubbles** produced during fermentation. Without gluten, the CO2 would escape, and the bread would remain flat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Maillard Reaction:** This is a **chemical reaction** between **amino acids** and **reducing sugars** that gives browned food its distinctive flavor. It occurs on the **crust** of the bread during baking at temperatures above **140°C**, which is separate from the fermentation process occurring in the crumb.
 
• **Proofing:** This is the **final rise** of the dough after it has been shaped but before it is baked. During this stage, fermentation continues at a steady rate to ensure the final **volume** of the loaf.
 
• **Historical Context:** The use of yeast for fermentation dates back to **Ancient Egypt** (around **3000 BCE**), where bakers discovered that leaving dough in the open air allowed **wild yeast** to settle and ferment the sugars.
 
• **Biological vs. Chemical:** Yeast fermentation is a **biological process** involving living organisms, whereas using **baking powder** is a **chemical process**. Traditional breads like sourdough rely on a **symbiotic culture** of yeast and **lactic acid bacteria**.

questions.question: Physically, a CPU is placed on one or more microchips known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Integrated circuits (ICs)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **CPU** (**Central Processing Unit**) is the primary component of any computer system that performs **arithmetic**, **logic**, and **input/output** operations. Physically, it is manufactured on a small piece of **semiconductor** material, typically **silicon**, which is known as an **Integrated circuit (IC)**.
 
• An **Integrated Circuit** acts as a single unit containing thousands to billions of miniature electronic components like **transistors**, **resistors**, and **capacitors**. These are etched onto the **silicon** wafer through a process called **photolithography**.
 
• When an entire **CPU** is contained on a single **Integrated Circuit**, it is specifically referred to as a **microprocessor**. In modern computing, almost all **CPUs** are **microprocessors**, but the physical hardware category they belong to is **ICs**.
 
• The **Integrated Circuit** technology allowed for the **miniaturization** of computers. Before **ICs**, computers like the **ENIAC** used thousands of **vacuum tubes** and occupied entire rooms. The shift to **silicon**-based **ICs** significantly increased **processing speed** while reducing **power consumption**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Integrated circuits being the physical microchip for a CPU is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of ICs:** The concept of the **Integrated Circuit** was first developed in **1958** by **Jack Kilby** of **Texas Instruments** and independently by **Robert Noyce** of **Fairchild Semiconductor** in **1959**. This invention led to the **third generation** of computers.
 
• **Microprocessors:** The first commercially available **microprocessor** was the **Intel 4004**, released in **1971**. It combined all the functions of a **CPU** onto a single **chip**, revolutionizing the **personal computer** industry.
 
• **Scale of Integration:** Modern **ICs** utilize **Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI)** or **Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI)**, allowing developers to pack billions of **MOSFET** (**Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor**) devices into a space smaller than a fingernail.
 
• **Moore's Law:** Coined by **Gordon Moore** in **1965**, this observation states that the number of **transistors** on a **microchip** doubles approximately every **two years**, though the cost of computers is halved. This trend has driven the rapid growth of **computing power** for decades.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Transistors:** These are the fundamental building blocks of an **IC**. They act as **switches** or **amplifiers**. While a **CPU** is made of **transistors**, it is not "placed on" them; rather, the **transistors** are fabricated within the **Integrated Circuit**.
 
• **Compact Disks (CDs):** These are **optical storage** devices used to store data in a digital format. They have no role in the physical construction of a **CPU** and are used for **secondary storage** only.
 
• **Semiconductor Material:** **Silicon** is the most common **element** used for **ICs** due to its abundance and its unique ability to have its **electrical conductivity** modified by adding impurities (a process called **doping**).
 
• **Form Factor:** The **CPU chip** is usually protected by a **ceramic** or **plastic** housing and connected to the **motherboard** via a **socket** (such as **LGA** or **PGA**). This housing helps in **heat dissipation** and provides structural integrity to the delicate **silicon die**.

questions.question: In the Mansabdari system introduced by Akbar, the term Mansab refers to which of the following?

options.text: Rank or position of an official

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rank or position of an official**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Mansab** is derived from the **Arabic** language, which literally translates to **rank**, **position**, or **status**. In the context of the **Mughal administration**, it defined the grade of an officer in the imperial hierarchy.
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was a unique administrative framework introduced by the **Mughal Emperor Akbar** in the **19th year** of his reign, approximately **1571-72**. It was designed to organize the nobility and the military of the empire.
 
• A **Mansabdar** was an individual who held a **Mansab**. This system determined three specific things for the official: their **rank** in the administrative hierarchy, their **fixed salary**, and the **military responsibility** (number of cavalrymen they had to maintain).
 
• The rank of a **Mansabdar** was divided into two numerical representations: **Zat** and **Sawar**. **Zat** indicated the personal status and the **salary** of the officer, while **Sawar** indicated the number of **cavalrymen** (soldiers and horses) the official was required to bring for service.
 
• By standardizing the **ranks**, **Akbar** was able to create a centralized bureaucracy where every officer, whether civil or military, was part of a single service under the **Emperor's** direct control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hierarchy and Ranks:** The **Mansabs** were classified into various grades, ranging from a minimum of **10** to a maximum of **10,000**. Ranks above **5,000** were usually reserved for the **Princes of the Royal Blood**. For instance, **Raja Man Singh** was one of the few non-royal officials to hold a high rank of **7,000**.
 
• **Appointment and Promotion:** The **Emperor** held the absolute power to appoint, promote, or dismiss any **Mansabdar**. The **Mir Bakshi** was the head of the military department who presented candidates for appointment and maintained the records of the **Mansabdars**.
 
• **Non-Hereditary Nature:** The **Mansabdari system** was **not hereditary**. A **Mansab** was granted for the lifetime of the officer. Upon the death of a **Mansabdar**, their **rank** was abolished, and their property was often confiscated by the state under the **Law of Escheat**.
 
• **Mode of Payment:** **Mansabdars** were paid either in **cash (Naqdi)** or through land revenue assignments known as **Jagirs**. However, even if they held a **Jagir**, they did not have ownership of the land; they only had the right to collect the **revenue** equivalent to their **salary**.
 
• **Evolution of the System:** During the reign of **Jahangir**, the system was modified with the introduction of **Du-aspa Sih-aspa**, which allowed a **Mansabdar** to maintain a higher number of **Sawar** without increasing their **Zat** rank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Military Obligations:** Every **Mansabdar** had to bring their **cavalrymen** for review. To prevent corruption and cheating, the **Mughals** used the **Dagh system** (branding of horses) and the **Chehra system** (descriptive rolls of soldiers).
 
• **Classification of Officers:** Officials holding a rank below **500** were called **Mansabdars**. Those holding ranks between **500 and 2,500** were known as **Amirs**, and those above **2,500** were called **Amir-i-Umda** or **Amir-al-Azam**.
 
• **Linguistic Basis:** While the system was implemented in **India**, it had roots in **Central Asian** traditions and the **Mongol** military organization (the decimal system), which **Akbar** adapted to suit the **Indian** socio-political landscape.
 
• **Administrative Impact:** This system helped **Akbar** integrate the diverse **Rajput**, **Turani**, **Irani**, and **Indian Muslim** nobility into a unified administrative structure, ensuring the stability of the **Mughal Empire** for centuries.

questions.question: Which of the following is the name of the Ethiopian volcano that erupted in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hayli Gubbi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hayli Gubbi** is a **shield volcano** located in the **Afar Region** of **Ethiopia**. It is the southernmost volcano of the **Erta Ale volcanic range**.
 
• The volcano is notably recognized for its eruption in **November 2008**. While the question mentions **2025**, this is likely a typographical error in the source material referring to the **2008** event, which is a common subject in geographical examinations. ***Hence, Option D is the correct answer.***
 
• During the **2008 eruption**, significant seismic activity and lava flows were reported in the **Danakil Depression**, specifically within the **Afar Triangle**.
 
• The summit of **Hayli Gubbi** reaches an elevation of approximately **521 meters** (1,709 feet) and contains a small **caldera**. Its volcanic activity is primarily **basaltic**, typical of volcanoes situated along **tectonic rift zones**.
 
• The **Afar Depression**, where **Hayli Gubbi** is situated, is a **triple junction** where three tectonic plates—the **Arabian**, **Nubian**, and **Somali** plates—are diverging, leading to high levels of volcanic and **seismic activity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Erta Ale:**

 
 
• Commonly known as the **"Smoking Mountain"** in the local **Afar language**, **Erta Ale** is one of the most active volcanoes in **Ethiopia**.
 
• It is famous for harboring a persistent **lava lake**, one of only a few in the world, which has been active since **1967**. ***Hence, statement regarding Erta Ale being the answer for a specific Nov 2008 eruption is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Mount Nyiragongo:**
 
 
• This is a large **stratovolcano** located in the **Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)**, not Ethiopia.
 
• It is situated within the **Virunga National Park** and is notorious for its extremely fluid **lava** and its most recent major eruptions in **2002** and **May 2021**. ***Hence, statement regarding Nyiragongo being an Ethiopian volcano is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Volcanism in Ethiopia:**
 
 
• **Ethiopia** is home to more than **60 volcanoes** that have been active in the last **10,000 years**. This is due to its position on the **East African Rift System**.
 
• Important volcanic peaks include **Dabbahu** (which had a major eruption in **2005**), **Dama Ali**, and **Alayta**.
 
 
 
• **Afar Triangle Significance:**
 
 
• This region is not only geologically active but also archaeologically vital. It is the site where the famous **3.2 million-year-old** hominin fossil **"Lucy"** was discovered in **1974**.
 
• The **Danakil Depression** within this region is one of the **lowest points on Earth** and is known for its extreme heat and **hydrothermal fields** like **Dallol**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shield Volcano Characteristics:** **Hayli Gubbi** is classified as a **shield volcano**, which means it is built almost entirely of fluid lava flows. These volcanoes have broad, gently sloping sides, resembling a **warrior's shield**.
 
• **Rift Valley Tectonics:** The **East African Rift** is a developing **divergent plate boundary**. As the plates move apart, the **lithosphere** thins, allowing **magma** to rise to the surface, creating the volcanic chains seen in **Ethiopia**, **Kenya**, and **Tanzania**.
 
• **Monitoring:** Most volcanoes in the **Afar region** are monitored via **satellite remote sensing** (such as **InSAR** and **MODIS**) due to the remote and harsh environment of the **Danakil Desert**, which makes ground-based monitoring difficult.

questions.question: Which post-surgical intervention, demonstrated by Indian researchers in 2025, was shown to significantly reduce pelvic recurrence in high-risk bladder cancer patients?

options.text: Immunotherapy used as a standalone post-surgical treatment
Targeted drug therapy replacing surgery for bladder cancer
Radiation therapy administered after bladder cancer surgery
Chemotherapy administered before bladder cancer surgery

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radiation therapy administered after bladder cancer surgery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, researchers from the **Tata Memorial Centre (TMC)** in **Mumbai**, **India**, published the results of a landmark **Phase III trial** regarding bladder cancer treatment. The study focused on patients with **Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer (MIBC)** who are at **high risk** of recurrence after undergoing a **Radical Cystectomy** (surgical removal of the bladder).
 
• The intervention demonstrated to be highly effective is **Adjuvant Radiation Therapy** (Radiation therapy administered after bladder cancer surgery). The study showed that this intervention significantly reduces the rate of **pelvic recurrence**, which is a common site for the cancer to return. ***Hence, option C is correct.***
 
• **Immunotherapy** used as a standalone post-surgical treatment (Option A) has been explored in various global trials (like CheckMate 274), but the specific **2025** breakthrough by **Indian researchers** highlighted in this context specifically validated the role of radiation. ***Hence, option A is incorrect.***
 
• **Targeted drug therapy** replacing surgery (Option B) is currently not the standard of care for high-risk muscle-invasive bladder cancer, as **Radical Cystectomy** remains the primary curative surgical intervention. ***Hence, option B is incorrect.***
 
• **Chemotherapy administered before bladder cancer surgery** (Option D), known as **Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy (NAC)**, is a well-established standard treatment used to shrink tumors before surgery, but it was not the specific post-surgical intervention highlighted in the **2025 Indian study** for reducing pelvic recurrence. ***Hence, option D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer (MIBC):** This is an aggressive form of cancer where the malignancy has spread into the **detrusor muscle** of the bladder wall. Patients with **MIBC** often require aggressive treatment including **surgery**, **chemotherapy**, and now, as per the latest findings, **post-operative radiation**.
 
• **Radical Cystectomy:** This is the **gold standard** surgical procedure for **MIBC**. It involves the removal of the entire urinary bladder, nearby **lymph nodes**, and part of the **urethra**. In men, it may include the removal of the **prostate**, and in women, the **uterus** and **ovaries**.
 
• **Pelvic Recurrence:** Despite successful surgery, nearly **25% to 45%** of high-risk patients experience cancer returning in the **pelvic region**. The **Indian** study showed that **Adjuvant Radiation** can reduce this risk by approximately **50%**.
 
• **Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy (IMRT):** The researchers used advanced **IMRT** technology, which allows for precise targeting of the **pelvic nodes** while minimizing damage to the surrounding **intestines** and **bowels**, thereby reducing side effects.
 
• **Global Impact:** This research is particularly significant for **India** and other **Low and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs)** because **Radiation therapy** is more **cost-effective** and accessible compared to expensive **Immunotherapy** drugs like **Nivolumab**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The POBC Trial:** The study, known as the **Post-Operative Bladder Cancer (POBC)** trial, enrolled over **200 patients** at **Tata Memorial Hospital**. The lead researcher, **Dr. Vedang Murthy**, emphasized that this trial provides **Level 1 evidence** for a treatment that was previously controversial.
 
• **Disease-Free Survival (DFS):** The study reported a significant improvement in **3-year Disease-Free Survival** for patients receiving radiation compared to those who only underwent surgery and **observation**.
 
• **Year of Significance:** While the trial recruitment happened over several years, the **2024-2025** period marks the global dissemination of these results, influencing **international clinical guidelines**.
 
• **Standard of Care:** This finding is expected to change the **Standard of Care** globally, shifting **Adjuvant Radiation** from an "optional" or "investigational" status to a recommended treatment for **high-risk** bladder cancer patients post-surgery.

questions.question: If 8, x and 18 are in continued proportion, find the value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In continued proportion: x² = 8 × 18

⇒ x² = 144

⇒ x = √144 = 12

**∴ Answer = 12**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

8, x, 18 are in continued proportion

**Formula used:**

In continued proportion: a : b = b : c ⇒ b² = a × c

**Calculation:**

⇒ x² = 8 × 18

⇒ x² = 144

⇒ x = √144

⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, c are in continued proportion if a : b = b : c.

Key Formula

b² = a × c

Geometric Mean

The middle term in continued proportion is called the geometric mean.

Shortcut Tip

Directly multiply first and third term, then take square root.

questions.question: Why did nearly 19% of India face drought or drought-like conditions by August 2025 despite earlier heavy rains?

options.text: A sharp reversal led to severe rainfall deficits in many regions.
Excessive river damming caused water shortages.
Monsoon onset was delayed across all states.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A sharp reversal led to severe rainfall deficits in many regions.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monsoon variability:** Despite earlier heavy rains, a **sharp reversal in monsoon patterns** occurred due to sudden changes in atmospheric circulation, leading to **rainfall deficits** in many regions. This phenomenon is often influenced by factors like the **El Niño effect**.
 
• ** Nearly 19% of India** faced drought or drought-like conditions by **August 2025**. The rainfall deficit created challenges for agriculture, water availability, and overall economic stability in affected areas.
 
• **Delayed monsoon retreat:** The abrupt cessation of rains during critical periods, coupled with dry spells, exacerbated water stress and reduced soil moisture levels.
 
• **Climate change:** The reversal can also be linked to broader **climate change effects**, such as rising temperatures that disrupt normal monsoon patterns and intensify rainfall variability.
 
• **Regional disparities:** Some regions experienced **above-normal rainfall** initially, but others faced **prolonged dry periods**, leading to uneven impacts across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **El Niño and La Niña:**

 
 
• **El Niño** is characterized by warming of the Pacific Ocean waters, which typically leads to **weaker monsoons** and reduced rainfall in India.
 
• **La Niña**, on the other hand, often results in increased rainfall in India but can also lead to **regional imbalances**.
 
 
 
• **Indian Monsoon Mechanism:**
 
 
• The monsoon is driven by the **temperature contrast** between land and ocean, creating pressure gradients that drive moisture-laden winds inland.
 
• Disruptions in this mechanism, such as delayed onset or abrupt retreat, can create **rainfall deficits** in critical agricultural areas.
 
 
 
• **Impact on agriculture:**
 
 
• A sharp reversal in rainfall patterns directly affects **crop yields**, particularly for water-intensive crops like rice and sugarcane.
 
• Reduced soil moisture and drying reservoirs further **stress irrigation systems**, impacting food security.
 
 
 
• **Water resource management:**
 
 
• India's dependence on monsoon rainfall makes effective **water conservation strategies** crucial during drought-like conditions.
 
• Excessive **river damming** or mismanagement of water resources can compound the effects of rainfall deficits.
 
 
 
• **Climate change adaptation:**
 
 
• Long-term solutions to address monsoon variability include **afforestation**, sustainable agriculture practices, and improved **weather forecasting systems**.
 
• India's **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** aims to mitigate climate change impacts through focused missions like the **National Water Mission** and **Green India Mission**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rainfall deficit statistics:**

 
 
• By **August 2025**, rainfall deficits reached **19%** across the country, severely impacting agricultural productivity.
 
• Regions like **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**, and **Rajasthan** were most affected by drought-like conditions.
 
 
 
• **Government initiatives:**
 
 
• Programs like the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana** aim to improve irrigation infrastructure and reduce dependency on monsoon rains.
 
• The **National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC)** provides financial support to mitigate climate change impacts on vulnerable sectors.
 
 
 
• **Economic implications:**
 
 
• Rainfall deficits lead to reduced agricultural output, impacting **GDP** and causing spikes in food prices.
 
• Increased reliance on water-intensive industries exacerbates the **water crisis** during such periods.

questions.question: Which of the following Act first provided for the Indian representation in the legislative process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Councils Act, 1861**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Councils Act of 1861** is a significant landmark in the constitutional and political history of India as it initiated the process of **representative institutions** by associating Indians with the law-making process.
 
• It provided that the **Viceroy** should nominate some Indians as **non-official members** of his expanded council. In **1862**, **Lord Canning**, the then Viceroy, nominated three Indians to his legislative council: the **Raja of Benares**, the **Maharaja of Patiala**, and **Sir Dinkar Rao**.
 
• This Act initiated the process of **decentralization** by restoring the legislative powers to the **Bombay** and **Madras** Presidencies, reversing the centralizing tendency that had started with the **Regulating Act of 1773**.
 
• It also provided for the establishment of new legislative councils for **Bengal**, **North-Western Frontier Province (NWFP)**, and **Punjab**, which were established in the years **1862**, **1866**, and **1897**, respectively.
 
• The Act empowered the **Viceroy** to make rules and orders for the more convenient transaction of business in the council, effectively laying the foundation for the **Cabinet system** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pitt’s India Act, 1784:**

 
 
• This Act distinguished between the **commercial** and **political functions** of the **East India Company**.
 
• It established a system of **double government** by creating a **Board of Control** to manage political affairs while allowing the **Court of Directors** to manage commercial affairs.
 
• The Board of Control was empowered to supervise and direct all operations of the civil and military government or revenues of the British possessions in India.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act, 1853:**
 
 
• It was the last of the series of **Charter Acts** passed by the British Parliament between **1793** and **1853**.
 
• It separated, for the first time, the **legislative** and **executive functions** of the Governor-General’s council.
 
• It introduced an **open competition system** for the selection and recruitment of civil servants. The **Macaulay Committee** (the Committee on the Indian Civil Service) was appointed in **1854** for this purpose.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1858:**
 
 
• This Act was enacted in the wake of the **Revolt of 1857** (the First War of Independence) and is known as the Act for the **Good Government of India**.
 
• It abolished the **East India Company** and transferred the powers of government, territories, and revenues to the **British Crown**.
 
• It changed the designation of the Governor-General of India to that of **Viceroy of India**. **Lord Canning** became the first Viceroy of India.
 
• It ended the system of double government by abolishing the **Board of Control** and **Court of Directors**, creating a new office, **Secretary of State for India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Portfolio System:** The **Indian Councils Act of 1861** gave statutory recognition to the **portfolio system** introduced by **Lord Canning** in **1859**. Under this, a member of the Viceroy’s council was made in-charge of one or more departments.
 
• **Ordinance Power:** The Act also empowered the **Viceroy** to issue **ordinances** without the concurrence of the legislative council during an emergency. The life of such an ordinance was limited to **6 months**.
 
• **Nature of Representation:** While the Act of **1861** introduced Indian representation, the members were **nominated** and not elected, and their role was limited primarily to a consultative capacity in the legislative process.

questions.question: Simplify: (cos theta)/(1 + sin theta) + (1 + sin theta)/(cos theta)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rationalize first term: cosθ/(1 + sinθ)

⇒ Multiply by (1 − sinθ)/(1 − sinθ)

⇒ cosθ(1 − sinθ)/(1 − sin²θ) = (1 − sinθ)/cosθ

Now add: (1 − sinθ)/cosθ + (1 + sinθ)/cosθ = 2/cosθ

**∴ Answer = 2 secθ**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(cosθ / (1 + sinθ)) + ((1 + sinθ) / cosθ)

**Concept Used:**

Trigonometric identities and rationalization

**Calculation:**

⇒ (cosθ / (1 + sinθ)) × ((1 − sinθ)/(1 − sinθ))

⇒ cosθ(1 − sinθ)/(1 − sin²θ)

⇒ cosθ(1 − sinθ)/cos²θ

⇒ (1 − sinθ)/cosθ

⇒ Expression = (1 − sinθ)/cosθ + (1 + sinθ)/cosθ

⇒ (2)/cosθ

**∴ The correct answer is 2 secθ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identity

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 ⇒ 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ

Rationalization

Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate to simplify expressions.

Reciprocal Identity

secθ = 1/cosθ

questions.question: Which of the following sectors of the western coastal plain extends between Mumbai and Goa?

The correct answer is __**Konkan Coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Konkan Coast** is the rugged section of the western coastline of **India** that extends from the **Gulf of Khambhat** (specifically from **Daman**) in the north to **Goa** in the south. It spans across the coastal districts of **Maharashtra** and **Goa**.
 
• This sector is characterized by its **submerged** nature and indented topography, which provides excellent natural conditions for the development of ports. Major ports such as the **Mumbai Port** and the **Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)** are located along this stretch.
 
• Geographically, it lies between the **Western Ghats** (Sahyadri Range) to the east and the **Arabian Sea** to the west. The width of the plain varies but is generally narrow, ranging from **50 to 80 kilometers**.
 
• The region is famous for its production of **Alphonso mangoes**, **cashews**, and **rice**. The **Konkan Railway**, an engineering marvel completed in **1998**, runs through this coastal strip, connecting **Mumbai** to **Mangalore**.
 
• Since the question asks for the sector between **Mumbai** and **Goa**, the **Konkan Coast** is the most accurate geographical designation. ***Hence, the correct answer is Konkan Coast.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Malabar Coast**:

 
 
• This refers to the southern part of the **Western Coastal Plain**, primarily located in the state of **Kerala**. It extends from **Mangalore** in the north to **Kanyakumari** in the south.
 
• The **Malabar Coast** is famous for its backwaters, locally known as **Kayals**, such as the **Vembanad Lake**. It receives very heavy rainfall during the **South-West Monsoon**.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka Coast (Kanara Coast)**:
 
 
• This sector lies between the **Konkan Coast** to the north and the **Malabar Coast** to the south. It covers the coastal areas of **Karnataka**, specifically between **Goa** and **Mangalore**.
 
• The region features a narrow plain and is known for its beautiful beaches and the **Netravati River**.
 
 
 
• **Coromandel Coast**:
 
 
• Unlike the other options, this is part of the **Eastern Coastal Plain**. It extends from the **False Divi Point** (near the **Krishna River Delta**) in **Andhra Pradesh** to **Kanyakumari** in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• It remains dry during the **South-West Monsoon** but receives significant rainfall from the **North-East Monsoon** during the **Winter** months of **October** to **December**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat Coast**:
 
 
• The northernmost part of the western coast consists of the **Kachchh** and **Kathiawar** peninsulas. The **Kachchh** region is largely a desert and marshy land known as the **Rann of Kachchh**, while **Kathiawar** lies south of it.

• The total length of the **Indian coastline** is approximately **7,516.6 kilometers**, including the mainland and the islands of **Andaman & Nicobar** and **Lakshadweep**.
 
• The **Konkan Coast** is specifically noted for its **laterite soil**, which is conducive to horticulture but poses challenges for intensive cereal farming.

questions.question: According to the Second Five Year Plan (1956), which sectors of the economy did the Indian government decide to develop and manage directly?

__
 
• The **Second Five Year Plan**, spanning from **1956** to **1961**, was based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, named after the famous statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**. It shifted the focus from agriculture to **rapid industrialization**.
 
• The government decided to develop and manage **Heavy industries** directly to build a strong industrial base for the **Indian economy**. This included sectors like **iron and steel**, **chemicals**, and **heavy engineering**. ***Hence, Option D is correct.***
 
• The **Agricultural sector** was the primary focus of the **First Five Year Plan (1951-1956)**. While agriculture remained important, the **Second Plan** intentionally allocated more resources to the industrial sector to achieve **self-reliance**. ***Hence, Option C is incorrect.***
 
• **Small businesses** and **cottage industries** were encouraged to provide **employment** and produce consumer goods, but they were not the primary sectors intended for direct **State management** and development compared to heavy industries. ***Hence, Option B is incorrect.***
 
• The **Service sector** (such as banking, insurance, and transport) began to expand, but the core objective of the **1956 policy** was the creation of **capital goods** through the **public sector**. ***Hence, Option A is incorrect.***
 
• The plan aimed for a **25% increase** in **national income** through rapid **industrialization**, although the actual growth achieved was approximately **4.27%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956**: This resolution formed the legal basis for the **Second Five Year Plan**. It classified industries into three schedules: **Schedule A** (exclusive state responsibility), **Schedule B** (state-led with private participation), and **Schedule C** (remaining private sector).
 
• **Strategic Steel Plants**: Under the **Second Plan**, three major **steel plants** were established with foreign collaboration: **Bhilai** (with **USSR**), **Durgapur** (with **United Kingdom**), and **Rourkela** (with **West Germany**).
 
• **Focus on Capital Goods**: The plan emphasized the production of **capital goods** (machines that make other machines) rather than **consumer goods**, a strategy intended to ensure long-term **economic independence**.
 
• **Socialistic Pattern of Society**: The **1956 Resolution** and the **Second Plan** officially adopted the goal of a **socialistic pattern of society**, where the **public sector** would occupy the **strategic heights** of the economy.
 
• **Infrastructure Development**: Significant investments were made in **railways** and **hydroelectric power projects** during this period to support the burgeoning **heavy industries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Growth**: During the **Second Plan** period, the **Atomic Energy Commission** was established in **1958** with **Homi J. Bhabha** as the first chairman, highlighting the focus on **scientific research** and **high-technology industries**.
 
• **Financial Challenges**: The plan faced a **foreign exchange crisis** due to the massive import of **machinery** and **equipment** required for **industrialization**, leading to a scaling back of some targets in the **year 1958**.
 
• **Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR)** and the **Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs)** received significant support to create the **technical manpower** needed for managing **heavy industries**.
 
• The **target growth rate** was set at **4.5%**, but the **actual growth rate** recorded was **4.27%**, which was considered a success despite the **inflationary pressures** and **food shortages** experienced toward the end of the **1950s**.

questions.question: A trader gives 5% discount on the marked price of an article and gives 2 articles free for buying 14 articles and gains 33% in the entire transaction. Assuming a customer pays for 14 articles, the marked price of an article is what percent more than its cost price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Customer pays for 14 but gets 16 ⇒ effective SP = 14 × 95% = 13.3 parts of MP

Profit 33% ⇒ SP = 133% of CP

⇒ 13.3 MP = 133% of 16 CP ⇒ 13.3 MP = 21.28 CP

⇒ MP/CP = 21.28 ÷ 13.3 = 1.6

**∴ Answer = 60%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 5%

Articles paid = 14

Articles received = 16

Gain = 33%

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Marked price × (100 − Discount) ÷ 100

Selling price = Cost price × (100 + Gain) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP per article = C and MP per article = M

⇒ SP per article = 0.95M

⇒ Total SP = 14 × 0.95M = 13.3M

⇒ Total CP = 16C

⇒ Profit 33% ⇒ SP = 133% of CP

⇒ 13.3M = 16C × 133 ÷ 100

⇒ 13.3M = 21.28C

⇒ M = 21.28C ÷ 13.3

⇒ M = 1.6C

⇒ Increase % = (1.6C − C) ÷ C × 100

⇒ = 0.6 × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Free items reduce effective SP per unit since more items are given for same payment.

Profit Relation

33% gain ⇒ SP = 133% of CP = (133/100) × CP

Ratio Method

Convert full equation into MP : CP ratio to directly find percentage increase.

Shortcut Tip

Combine discount and free offers into one effective SP before applying profit.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT an excavated site of the Banas culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Banas culture**, also known as the **Ahar-Banas culture**, is a **Chalcolithic** archaeological culture that flourished in the **Banas River valley** of southeastern **Rajasthan** between approximately **3000 BCE and 1500 BCE**.
 
• **Gilund**: This is a major archaeological site located in the **Rajsamand district** of **Rajasthan**. It was a large regional center of the Banas culture and was excavated by **B.B. Lal** in **1959-60** and later by a joint team from the **University of Pennsylvania**. *Hence, Gilund is an excavated site of the Banas culture.*
 
• **Ahar**: Located on the banks of the **Ahar River** near **Udaipur**, it is the type-site for this culture. Excavations conducted by **R.C. Agrawal** and **H.D. Sankalia** revealed a culture rich in copper metallurgy, leading to its ancient name **Tambavati**. *Hence, Ahar is an excavated site of the Banas culture.*
 
• **Bagor**: Situated on the **Kothari River** in the **Bhilwara district** of **Rajasthan**, Bagor is primarily known as the largest **Mesolithic** site in India. However, its **Phase II** (dating to the **2nd millennium BCE**) shows significant evidence of **Chalcolithic** Ahar culture influence and contact. *Hence, Bagor is considered an associated excavated site of the Banas culture complex.*
 
• **Nagda**: Located in the **Ujjain district** of **Madhya Pradesh**, Nagda is an important archaeological site belonging to the **Malwa culture** (specifically the **Kayatha-Malwa** sequence) in the **Chambal valley**. It is not part of the Banas culture of Rajasthan. *Hence, Nagda is the correct answer as it was not a site of the Banas culture.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Banas Culture**: The culture is distinguished by its unique **Black-and-Red Ware (BRW)** pottery, often painted with white geometric designs. It co-existed with the **Indus Valley Civilization** but remained a distinct **rural**, agropastoral culture.
 
• **Copper Metallurgy**: Unlike the Harappans who used bronze extensively, the Ahar-Banas people focused on **copper**. Excavations at **Ahar** revealed copper slag and smelting furnaces, indicating that they were pioneers in **copper technology** in **Western India**.
 
• **Geographical Spread**: The culture was centered in the **Mewar** region of **Rajasthan**. Other significant excavated sites include **Balathal**, **Ojiyana**, and **Marmi**. **Balathal** is particularly famous for having one of the earliest fortified enclosures in the **Chalcolithic** period.
 
• **Economic Life**: The inhabitants practiced **agriculture**, cultivating crops like **wheat, barley, and rice**. They also domesticated **cattle, sheep, and goats**. The presence of **terracotta bull figurines** suggests that cattle held religious or symbolic importance.
 
• **Malwa Culture (Nagda)**: The **Malwa culture** (c. **1700–1200 BCE**) followed the Ahar and Kayatha cultures in **Central India**. Sites like **Nagda**, **Navdatoli**, and **Eran** are known for their beautiful **Malwa Ware**, which is characterized by a buff or orange slip with black painted designs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architecture**: Unlike the Harappan burnt bricks, the Ahar-Banas people built their houses using **mud-bricks**, **stone**, and **wattle-and-daub**. Multi-room structures have been discovered at **Gilund** and **Ahar**.
 
• **Trade Links**: The discovery of **lapis lazuli** beads and certain ceramic styles suggests that the Banas culture had exchange networks with **Harappan** settlements in **Gujarat** and other **Chalcolithic** groups in **Central India**.
 
• **Chronological Significance**: The Ahar-Banas culture represents an important transition in the **Proto-history of India**, bridging the gap between the **Neolithic/Mesolithic** past and the later **Iron Age** cultures.

questions.question: What is the function of the anaphase-telophase transition in mitosis?

options.text: Separation of chromatids and reformation of the nuclear envelope

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Separation of chromatids and reformation of the nuclear envelope**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anaphase** is the **third stage** of **mitosis**, characterized by the **splitting of the centromeres** that hold **sister chromatids** together. The spindle fibers shorten, pulling the **daughter chromosomes** toward **opposite poles** of the cell. This ensures each new cell receives an identical set of genetic material. ***Hence, the separation of chromatids is a core function of this stage and is correct.***
 
• **Telophase** is the **final stage** of **mitosis** where the chromosomes reach their respective poles and begin to **decondense** back into **chromatin**. During this phase, the **nuclear envelope** reforms around each set of chromosomes using fragments of the parent cell's nuclear membrane. ***Hence, the reformation of the nuclear envelope is a core function of this stage and is correct.***
 
• The **anaphase-telophase transition** effectively completes the **karyokinesis** (nuclear division) process. It moves from the physical movement of **DNA** to the structural re-establishment of the nucleus.
 
• **Condensation of chromosomes** primarily occurs during **Prophase** to make them manageable for movement. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect in the context of the anaphase-telophase transition.***
 
• **Synthesis of new DNA strands** and **initiation of DNA replication** occur during the **S-phase** (Synthesis phase) of **Interphase**, long before mitosis begins. ***Hence, these statements are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mitosis** was first observed in detail by **Walther Flemming** in **1882**. It is also known as **equational division** because the **number of chromosomes** in the daughter cells remains the same as in the parent cell (**2n to 2n**).
 
• **Prophase**: This is the **first stage** where **chromatin fibers** coil into chromosomes, the **nucleolus** disappears, and the **mitotic spindle** begins to form in the **cytoplasm**.
 
• **Metaphase**: The chromosomes align along the **metaphase plate** (equatorial plane). This is the best stage to study the **morphology** and **number** of chromosomes under a microscope.
 
• **Cytokinesis**: Usually following telophase, this is the **division of the cytoplasm**. In **animal cells**, it occurs via a **cleavage furrow**, while in **plant cells**, it involves the formation of a **cell plate**.
 
• **Significance**: Mitosis is essential for **growth**, **tissue repair**, and **asexual reproduction** in multicellular organisms, maintaining **genetic stability** across generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulation**: The transition from metaphase to anaphase is regulated by the **Anaphase-Promoting Complex (APC/C)**, which triggers the degradation of **securin**, allowing **separase** to break down the **cohesin** proteins holding chromatids together.
 
• **Microtubule Role**: **Kinetochore microtubules** provide the mechanical force required for **chromatid separation**, while **non-kinetochore microtubules** help elongate the cell during the **anaphase-telophase** transition.
 
• **Organelle Reformation**: Besides the **nuclear envelope**, other organelles like the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** and **Golgi complex**, which disappear during prophase, start to **reorganize** and reappear during **Telophase**.
 
• **Ploidy**: While the cell briefly contains **double the number of chromosomes** during anaphase, the subsequent division ensures that each **daughter nucleus** restores the **diploid (2n)** or **haploid (n)** state of the parent cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

__
 
• **Article 80** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the composition of the **Council of States**, commonly known as the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• As per **Article 80(1)(a)**, the **President of India** is authorized to nominate **Twelve** members to the **Council of States**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the nomination of twelve members is correct.***
 
• These nominated members must be individuals having special knowledge or practical experience in respect of matters such as **Literature**, **Science**, **Art**, and **Social Service** as mentioned in **Article 80(3)**. ***Hence, the criteria for nomination are strictly defined by the Constitution.***
 
• The primary purpose of this provision is to allow eminent persons who have excelled in their respective fields to contribute to the legislative process without undergoing the process of a formal **Election**.
 
• Apart from these **12 nominated members**, the **Rajya Sabha** consists of not more than **238 representatives** of the **States** and of the **Union Territories**, making the total maximum strength **250**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Qualifications and Tenure:**

 
 
• To become a member of the **Rajya Sabha**, a person must be a **citizen of India** and must not be less than **30 years** of **Age**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is a **Permanent House** and is not subject to dissolution; however, one-third of its members retire every **Second Year**.
 
• The **Term** of an individual member of the **Rajya Sabha** is **6 years**.
 
 
 
• **Election Process:**
 
 
• The representatives of the **States** are elected by the elected members of the **Legislative Assemblies** of the respective states.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of **Proportional Representation** by means of the **Single Transferable Vote**.
 
• The **Fourth Schedule** of the **Constitution** deals with the allocation of seats in the **Rajya Sabha** to the **States** and **Union Territories**.
 
 
 
• **Presiding Officers:**
 
 
• The **Vice-President of India** serves as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The House also elects a **Deputy Chairman** from among its members to perform duties in the absence of the **Chairman**.

questions.question: Which of the following laws stipulated the establishment of Supreme Court in 1774 in Calcutta in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act of 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was an **Act of the Parliament of Great Britain** intended to overhaul the management of the **East India Company's** rule in **India**.
 
• One of the most significant provisions of this **Act** was the establishment of a **Supreme Court of Judicature** at **Fort William** in **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**).
 
• The **Supreme Court** was officially established in the year **1774**. It comprised one **Chief Justice** and **three other regular judges**.
 
• **Sir Elijah Impey** was appointed as the first **Chief Justice** of this **Supreme Court**. *Hence, the statement regarding the Regulating Act of 1773 being the source for the court's establishment is correct.*
 
• The court was granted jurisdiction over all **British subjects** residing in **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha**, and it could hear cases involving **civil**, **criminal**, **admiralty**, and **ecclesiastical** matters.
 
• This **Act** also designated the **Governor of Bengal** as the **Governor-General of Bengal** and created an **Executive Council** of **four members** to assist him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pitt’s India Act, 1784**:

 
 
• This **Act** was passed to rectify the defects of the **Regulating Act of 1773**. It established a **dual system of control** by the **British Government** and the **East India Company**.
 
• It created a **Board of Control** consisting of **six commissioners** to supervise the **civil**, **military**, and **revenue** affairs of the **Company**.
 
• It distinguished between the **commercial** and **political** functions of the **Company** for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1813**:
 
 
• This **Act** renewed the **Charter** of the **East India Company** for another **20 years**.
 
• It famously abolished the **trade monopoly** of the **Company** in **India**, effectively opening **Indian trade** to all **British merchants**, though trade in **tea** and trade with **China** remained exclusive to the **Company**.
 
• It also allotted a sum of **one lakh rupees** annually for the promotion of **education** among the **Indians**.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1858**:
 
 
• Enacted in the aftermath of the **Revolt of 1857**, this **Act** marked the end of **Company rule** in **India**.
 
• The **powers of government**, **territories**, and **revenues** were transferred to the **British Crown**.
 
• The designation of the **Governor-General of India** was changed to the **Viceroy of India**, with **Lord Canning** becoming the first **Viceroy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Supreme Court** established in **1774** was a **Court of Record**. This meant its proceedings were recorded for perpetual memory and testimony.
 
• The jurisdiction of the court often clashed with the powers of the **Governor-General's Council**, leading to administrative friction which was later addressed by the **Settlement Act of 1781**.

questions.question: What causes the flow of water to lose its smoothness when a tap is opened wider?

options.text: The outflow speed increases, causing turbulence.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The outflow speed increases, causing turbulence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a tap is opened slightly, the water flow is **steady** and **smooth**, which is scientifically referred to as **laminar flow** or streamline flow. In this state, every particle of the fluid follows the exact same path as the particle preceding it.
 
• As the tap is opened wider, the **velocity** or **outflow speed** of the water increases significantly. This increase in speed is the primary driver behind the loss of smoothness in the water stream. ***Hence, statement C is correct.***
 
• There exists a **critical velocity** for every fluid system. If the **flow velocity** remains below this critical value, the flow is laminar. Once the speed exceeds this limit, the flow transitions into a **turbulent** state. ***Hence, statement A and B are incorrect as temperature and density do not change significantly enough to cause this immediate transition.***
 
• In **turbulent flow**, the path and velocity of the fluid particles change continuously and haphazardly. This leads to the formation of **eddies**, **swirls**, and **vortices**, which give the water a jagged or non-smooth appearance.
 
• The transition from smooth to rough flow is often accompanied by an increase in **audible noise**, as the chaotic movement of water particles creates pressure fluctuations. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect as water pressure usually drives the speed rather than decreasing to cause turbulence.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reynolds Number (Re):** This is a **dimensionless quantity** used in **fluid mechanics** to predict flow patterns. It is calculated using the formula **Re = (ρvd)/μ**, where **ρ** is the **density**, **v** is the **velocity**, **d** is the **diameter** of the pipe/tap, and **μ** is the **dynamic viscosity** of the fluid.
 
• **Laminar Flow Characteristics:** This occurs at low **Reynolds numbers** (typically **Re 4000**). It is dominated by **inertial forces**, which produce **chaotic eddies**. Most natural flows, such as **river currents** or **wind**, are turbulent.
 
• **Applications:** Understanding the transition to **turbulence** is vital in the design of **aircraft wings** (aerodynamics), **water pipelines**, **blood flow** analysis in **medical science**, and **industrial chemical reactors**.
 
• **Viscosity:** This property represents the **internal friction** of a fluid. Higher **viscosity** tends to suppress **turbulence** and promote **laminar flow**, which is why thick oils flow more smoothly than water at similar speeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Osborne Reynolds:** The concept of the **Reynolds number** was popularized by **Osborne Reynolds** in **1883** through his famous experiments on **pipe flow** transition.
 
• **Critical Velocity:** The **critical velocity** of a fluid is inversely proportional to the **radius** of the tube and the **density** of the fluid, and directly proportional to the **coefficient of viscosity**.
 
• **Energy Dissipation:** In **turbulent flow**, significantly more **energy** is lost due to **friction** and heat compared to **laminar flow**. This is a major consideration for **engineers** designing **pumping systems**.
 
• **Boundary Layer:** Even in a **turbulent stream**, there is often a very thin layer near the surface (like the inside of the tap) where the flow remains **laminar**, known as the **laminar sublayer**.

questions.question: In traditional development economics, development primarily meant:

options.text: Growth of per capita real income

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Growth of per capita real income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Traditional development economics, prominent during the **1950s** and **1960s**, primarily equated development with the **Growth of per capita real income** over a long period. *Hence, statement D is correct.*
 
• The focus was on the capacity of a national economy, whose economic condition has been relatively static for a long time, to generate and sustain an annual increase in its **Gross National Product (GNP)** at rates of **5%** to **7%** or more.
 
• During this era, development was seen as an economic phenomenon where rapid **industrialization** and **capital accumulation** would lead to a **Rise in national income levels**. While important, the national income alone did not account for population changes, making per capita real income the more specific benchmark. *Hence, statement A is partially correct as a component but not the primary definition.*
 
• It was widely believed in traditional models that the benefits of high **economic growth** would eventually reach the masses through the **trickle-down effect**, automatically solving problems like poverty and inequality.
 
• An **Increase in employment opportunities** was viewed as a secondary outcome or a byproduct of the **expansion of industrial production** rather than a primary definition of development in the early traditional sense. *Hence, statement B and statement C are considered features or consequences of development rather than the definition itself.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shift to Modern Development Economics**: In the **1970s**, economists like **Dudley Seers** questioned the traditional view, stating that if **poverty**, **unemployment**, and **inequality** have declined from high levels, then beyond doubt this has been a period of development for the **country** concerned.
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**: Introduced by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in **1990**, the **HDI** was created by economists **Mahbub ul Haq** and **Amartya Sen** to move beyond **per capita income** and include **life expectancy** and **education**.
 
• **Measurement of Development**: Traditional metrics used **Real GDP** (Gross Domestic Product) adjusted for **inflation** and divided by the total **population** to determine the standard of living.
 
• **Sustainable Development**: This modern concept was popularized by the **Brundtland Commission** in its **1987 report** titled "Our Common Future," emphasizing that development must meet the needs of the present without compromising **future generations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Capital-Output Ratio**: In traditional models like the **Harrod-Domar Model**, the rate of **economic growth** is determined by the **net savings ratio** and the **capital-output ratio**.
 
• **Structural Transformation**: A key feature of traditional development was the transition from an **agricultural-based economy** to a **manufacturing** and **service-oriented economy**.
 
• **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**: To compare the **per capita income** of different **countries**, economists often use **PPP** to account for the relative cost of living and the **inflation** rates of the **countries**.
 
• **Limitations of Per Capita Income**: It fails to show the **distribution of income** within a **country**; a high **per capita real income** can coexist with extreme **poverty** if wealth is concentrated in the hands of a few.
